text: The CoprGuard framework begins with the diffusion model watermark injection stage to safeguard image copyright.
A watermark image and a clean protected image are first supplied as inputs to the watermark encoder.
A frozen pre-trained encoder employs discrete wavelet transforms and an invertible neural network to embed the watermark into high-frequency sub-bands.
Following the inverse transform, the encoder produces the watermarked image while discarding high-frequency residual artifacts.
These watermarked images are then incorporated into diffusion model training datasets.
In standard diffusion models, the denoising U-Net learns to reconstruct the watermarked image from noise, absorbing its underlying frequency properties.
In text-conditioned diffusion models, conditioning vectors guide the network during training, embedding identifiable watermark signatures directly into the model.
